mentions.name: GamingCouch.com
mentions.description: A web-based local multiplayer party game platform with 20+ action-oriented competitive mini-games playable in the browser with no downloads or installs. Players use their phones as controllers (gamepads work too), games support up to 8 players in quick ~1-minute rounds, and language-based trivia or turn-based games are excluded. The platform also offers third-party development tools (currently in private beta) so game developers can build and publish their own party minigames, with the first third-party game already launched.
mentions.problem: Local multiplayer game nights involve too much hassle switching between different titles and connecting 4-8 controllers to one PC or console, and language-based party games like Jackbox don't work when the group includes people not fluent in English.
mentions.audience: Groups of friends at game nights playing local multiplayer party games; game developers creating third-party minigames for the platform.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Working on a web-based local multiplayer party game platform called GamingCouch.com.

The idea is simple: I love local multiplayer games and game nights but felt that there was always too much hassle with switching between different titles and connecting 4-8 controllers to one PC or console. Jackbox worked great but they relied too much on language and didn't work when the group had people not fluent in english.
mentions.author: ChaosOp

mentions.name: Gaming Couch
mentions.description: Web-based local multiplayer party game platform, described as a lovechild of Jackbox and Mario Party, in free early access with 20+ competitive mini-games. Players use their phones as controllers (gamepads work too), everything runs in the browser with no downloads or installs, and every game supports up to 8 players with quick ~1 minute action-based rounds; no language-based trivia or asynchronous turn-based games.
